source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:5 ('חקותי — plene the second vav, and the Masorah: NONE full like it in the Torah; the Ramah: this alone full, all other statutes-words doubly lean')
claim_en: THE ONE FULL STATUTES-WORD: חקותי ('because Abraham kept My charge, My commandments, MY STATUTES, and My laws') — the Torah's UNIQUE plene statutes-word, and the census turns it into geography: the nine lean חקתי tokens all live in LEVITICUS (18:4 through 26:43, builder-verified refs), the law-book keeps its statutes lean — the one full writing belongs to Abraham's obedience before the law was given.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:5 (the lean family)
claim_en: ...the lean family censused: bare חקתי — nine tokens, every one in Leviticus (Lev 18:4, 18:5, 18:26, 19:19, 19:37, 20:8, 20:22, 25:18, 26:43).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:3 ('הארצת defective — all the books; and its neighbor likewise; the Masorah: all the Torah lean, ONE plene — the famine in all the lands'; the Ramah and the Baal HaTurim concur)
claim_en: THE LANDS RUN LEAN UNTIL THE FAMINE: הארצת ('to you and your seed I will give all THESE LANDS') — defective here and in its neighbor-verse (26:3, 26:4, the Torah's only two tokens of the form), and the ONE plene הארצות in the whole Torah is Gen 41:54 — 'and the famine was in all THE LANDS': the promise writes the lands lean; the famine fills them out. The Kitzur rides the missing vav: given after six generations.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:3 (the one plene)
claim_en: ...the famine-verse's plene censused: הארצות once in the Torah, Joseph's famine alone.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:3-4 ('האל — one of EIGHT sevirin האלה: the presumers err in them'; the Masorah's list on this verse; Bereshit Rabbah 64 named)
claim_en: THE PRESUMED THESE, TWICE IN ONE PROMISE: האל ('all THESE lands' — the short demonstrative) — one of the Masorah's EIGHT sevirin sites (readers presume the long האלה; the letter refuses it), and this promise carries TWO of the eight back to back (26:3, 26:4). SNAPSHOT census: consonantal האל stands 12 times in the Torah — the EIGHT short demonstratives of the sevirin list (Gen 19:8, 19:25, 26:3, 26:4, Lev 18:27, Deut 4:42, 7:22, 19:11) plus four Name-tokens ('the God,' Gen 31:13, 46:3, Deut 7:9, 10:17): the sevirin class verified whole at the letter.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:4 (the second sevirin leg)
claim_en: ...the neighbor-verse's short THESE verified in the stream.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:7 (the Masorah + the Ramah: 'the maiden טבת מראה — lean, and NONE lean like it in the Torah; the rest plene'; the Hilleli/Jerusalem split recorded)
claim_en: THE BRIDE'S BEAUTY, LEAN AT HOME AND FULL AT GERAR: טובת ('for she was FAIR of appearance' — Isaac's fear-verse) — PLENE here, and the fair-of-appearance phrase's one LEAN writing in the Torah is Rebecca's own debut (טבת מראה, 24:16, the Masorah's unique): the same woman's beauty is written lean at the well and full in the danger-tale. SNAPSHOT census: טובת once (26:7); bare טבת twice — the debut (24:16) and the daughters of men (6:2, outside the appearance-phrase, as the Masorah's phrase-scope requires).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:7 (the lean tokens)
claim_en: ...the lean tokens censused: טבת twice — Gen 6:2 and Gen 24:16.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:2 ('שכן defective — and a derash rides it in Bereshit Rabbah 64'; the Yefeh Toar named)
claim_en: שכן ('DWELL in the land that I tell you') — written defective, and Bereshit Rabbah 64's derash rides the lean imperative (make the Presence DWELL — the shekhina-reading). SNAPSHOT: no vav.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:3 ('השבעה defective — and every oath-word in the Torah likewise; the printed Masorah corrected by the Ramah')
claim_en: השבעה ('I will establish THE OATH I swore to Abraham') — defective, one of the ten always-lean oath-nouns censused whole at frozen G40-03 (the oath-is-seven rule): the Beer Sheva oath returns to its heir written lean as ever.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:7 ('פן יהרגני — the heh with PATACH, not hataf patach: a resting half-vowel cannot follow a compound one')
claim_en: יהרגני ('lest the men of the place KILL ME for Rebecca') — the heh in plain PATACH exactly as Minchat Shai's grammar demands (no compound half-vowel), and SNAPSHOT agrees: the fear-formula that ran plene at Gerar's last visit (והרגוני, 20:11, frozen G36-03) returns pointed as ruled.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:9 ('אחתי הוא — written with vav, as at Lech Lecha'); the pentateuchal written-he
claim_en: אחתי הוא ('she IS my sister... for I said: she IS...') — the she-word twice in Avimelech's sentence, both in the masculine skeleton with feminine vowels (the pentateuchal written-he), as the Masorah files it...

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:12 ('בשנה ההוא — written with vav; the Ramah: every masculine that-word vav-aleph, and the feminine likewise save the ELEVEN written yod-aleph')
claim_en: ...and בשנה ההוא ('Isaac sowed IN THAT YEAR, and reaped a hundredfold') — the feminine that-year written in the masculine vav-skeleton per the Ramah's rule; the rule's exception-list (his ELEVEN yod-aleph tokens) is the standing counted-law split against SNAPSHOT's eighteen (run 4's largest discrepancy, cited, not re-opened).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:10 ('מה זאת — the zayin DAGESHED')
claim_en: מה זאת ('WHAT IS THIS you have done to us?') — the zayin dageshed as ruled: Gerar's what-question carries the pressed letter, the third king to ask the garden's question of this family.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 26:10 ('אחד העם — two in the Masorah: here, and ONE OF THE PEOPLE came at Saul's spear — as there a king, so here')
claim_en: אחד העם ('ONE OF THE PEOPLE might easily have lain with your wife') — the pair stands ONCE in the Torah (adjacency-verified); the Masorah's second leg is David's whisper over sleeping Saul (I Sam 26:15; edge): 'as there the king himself, so here' — Avimelech means himself.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:14 ('ועבדה — defective after the bet'; Bereshit Rabbah 64: Daniel the tailor — 'if a man does not make himself as a slave to his work, he does not acquire it'); Kitzur: the Job pair
claim_en: ועבדה ('and a GREAT HOUSEHOLD of servants' — Isaac's Gerar wealth) — defective with the dageshed dalet, and Bereshit Rabbah's tailor-derash rides the lean word (read it AVODAH: no acquiring without serving); the form stands exactly TWICE in the Torah — here and the Levite's ceased service (Num 8:26); the Masorah's greatness-pair is Job's household (Job 1:3; edge).

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 26:15 ('וימלאום — two in the Masorah: the stopped wells, and the hundred foreskins FILLED to the king — measure for measure')
claim_en: וימלאום ('the Philistines stopped the wells AND FILLED THEM with earth') — UNIQUE in the Torah; the Masorah's pair-leg is David FILLING the foreskin-count to Saul (I Sam 18:27; edge): the Kitzur's measure-for-measure — Philistine earth into wells, Philistine forfeit doubled back.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 26:8 ('מצחק — two: Isaac LAUGHING with Rebecca; Ishmael the mocker — as here a wife, so there')
claim_en: מצחק ('Isaac LAUGHING with Rebecca his wife' — the window-scene) — exactly TWICE in the Torah: the husband's laughter here and Ishmael's mocking (21:9); the Kitzur reads the pair's grammar across: the laugh-word that undressed Ishmael's conduct names Isaac's marriage — same participle, opposite verdicts.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:8 ('ויהי כי — the כי under the WHEEL, not maqqef') + on 26:6 ('no lengthener on the yod') + on 26:12 ('the vav of ויברכהו with the lengthener')
claim_en: THE SMALL STROKES AS RULED: כי at 26:8 stands FREE of maqqef carrying its own conjunctive stroke (Minchat Shai names the galgal — the wheel — where SNAPSHOT's stream writes the plain servant-accent: the standing wheel-layer gap, named); וישב ('and Isaac DWELT,' 26:6) with NO lengthener on the yod, as ruled; ויברכהו ('and YHWH BLESSED HIM,' 26:12) with the lengthener on the vav, as ruled.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 26:12 (the lengthener leg)
claim_en: ...the blessing-verb's vav-stroke verified in the stream.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 64:4
claim_en: A NUMERIC CLAIM OPENED UNDER GUARD 3, AND THE ARITHMETIC HOLDS. Reish Lakish reads the opening word of 26:5 for its numeric value and gets 172, which subtracted from Abraham's 175 years yields three - the age at which he is said to have recognized his Creator. Computed at derivation from our own consonants: the word's three letters total exactly 172, and 175 minus 172 is 3. R. Yochanan and R. Chanina's rival answer of forty-eight is recorded beside it, unreconciled. The same section also claims Abraham knew even the courtyard-joining rules, reading the verse's stacked law-words as the entire system known before Sinai.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 64:7
claim_en: A LABOUR MAXIM CARRIED ON A MISSING LETTER. At 26:14 the word for his household staff is written short, and Daniyel the tailor reads the short spelling as the rule that one who does not make himself LIKE A SLAVE to his slave does not acquire him. Machine-checked: our tree carries the defective form the reading requires. A maxim of service relations resting on one absent letter in a wealth inventory.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 64:3
claim_en: SANCTUARY LAW IS IMPORTED INTO GEOGRAPHY TO BIND ONE MAN TO THE LAND. R. Hoshaya reads the command to remain as an offering-law analogy: you are an unblemished burnt offering, and as an offering that leaves the curtains is disqualified, so you leaving the Land are disqualified. The dwelling command is separately read as a settlement instruction - plant, sow, graft - and as causing the Presence to dwell. A ritual disqualification rule governing a person's movement.

check.note: An offering-disqualification rule transferred to a person's geography as binding law.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 64:3
claim_en: A SHORT SPELLING IS READ AS A DELIVERY SCHEDULE. The demonstrative in 'these lands' is written in its short form, and the chain reads it two ways: as the MIGHTY lands, or as a partial grant - some now, the rest in the future. An eschatological timetable carried by the length of one word.

check.note: A spelling variant read as dividing a promise into present and future instalments.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 64:5
claim_en: A MODESTY-LAW CLUSTER IS SEATED ON ONE NARRATIVE VERB. From the word rendered 'playing' at 26:8 the chain derives R. Yochanan's ruling that conjugal relations belong to the night, with Esther cited as proof and daytime relations graded indecent; Job and Jeremiah cursing the day of their conception are brought as enforcement exhibits, and one prophet's exception - fleeing a queen's killings - is recorded rather than suppressed. The same verse also carries the rule that a bad dream, a harsh prophecy and disproportionate mourning are all nullified by length of days.

check.note: A cluster of conduct rulings derived from a single narrative verb, with its exception preserved.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 64:6
claim_en: A LIVE COLLISION BETWEEN TWO STANDING RULES IS RESOLVED ON THIS VERSE. Blessing does not rest on what is weighed, measured or counted - so why did he measure the hundredfold harvest? FOR THE TITHES. The measuring is permitted only because a tithing duty requires it. Two received rules meet on one narrative act and the narrative decides the priority.

check.note: Two standing rules in tension, adjudicated by appeal to a narrative act's purpose.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 73:8
claim_en: THIS VERSE IS ENROLLED AS THE FIRST MEMBER OF A BLESSING-BY-PROXIMITY CENSUS. Three are counted as having enriched the households they served or dwelt beside - Isaac at Gerar here, Jacob at Laban's, Joseph at Potiphar's - the census cited later out of Laban's own mouth. Our verse is the class's opening member.

check.note: A census of blessing-by-proximity whose first member is this verse and whose witness is a later antagonist.

source: Onkelos Genesis 26:5; Bereshit Rabbah 64:4
claim_en: BOTH MEMBERS READ THE VERSE MAXIMALLY, AND ONE OF THEM WRITES IT. Where the chain holds that Abraham kept the whole law-system before Sinai, Onkelos renders the verse's stacked terms in full rabbinic register - he RECEIVED MY WORD and kept the mandate of My Word, My commandments, My decrees and My TEACHINGS. The translation does not merely permit the maximal reading; it supplies the vocabulary that carries it.

check.note: A maximal legal reading stated by one member of the shelf and lexically enabled by the other.

source: Onkelos Genesis 26:3; Onkelos Genesis 26:12
claim_en: TWO STANDING TRANSLATION POLICIES FIRE IN THIS BLOCK. The presence-promise is routed through the Word - 'I will be with you' becomes MY WORD WILL BE YOUR SUPPORT, the standing buffer at covenant assurances. And the hundredfold is rendered as a hundred times WHAT THEY ESTIMATED IT, which is the estimate reading the midrash gives at the same verse - the two members converging on an agricultural measure without citation.

check.note: A reverence buffer at a covenant promise, plus an independent convergence on a quantitative reading.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 25:3; Bereshit Rabbah 64:2
claim_en: THIS FAMINE IS SEATED AS A MEMBER OF A STANDING CENSUS. The ten famines are counted across the corpus and 26:1 is the Isaac member, the verse marking itself with 'besides the first famine' - the text supplying its own cross-reference. The frame is recorded with it: the LORD will not starve the righteous, cashed as Isaac, against the averted devastation of the wicked, cashed as the king.

check.note: A corpus-wide census whose member here is flagged by the verse's own comparative clause.
